cc_premise_trace.argument: An exceptional null set restricted to [s,t] is enlarged only by its two endpoints. CC measure/volume suppliers make finite sets and finite unions null. AC restricts to subinterval families. One open U containing E with measure less than the AC modulus is obtained from the actual CC outer-regularity theorem.

At every good point the derivative-zero definition gives a positive radius. At bad points openness of U gives a positive radius. Geometric decay makes each corresponding set of natural indices nonempty; its unique least index defines the gauge by ordinary definable assignment. No arbitrary family of pointwise choices is selected.

If no fine partition exists, choose the left half when it is bad and otherwise the necessarily bad right half. This deterministic recursion needs no DC. Nested intervals and geometric lengths give a common point; a sufficiently small retained interval tagged at that point contradicts badness. The published degenerate-interval convention is explicit.

Bad-tag cells lie in U; their interiors are disjoint. Shared endpoints are a finite null set, so finite additivity and interval volume give total bad-cell length at most measure(U), strictly below the AC modulus. AC bounds their total endpoint increments; the empty family contributes zero.

Strict gauge containment puts both endpoints within the good tag radius. The tag lies in its cell, so the two distances add to its length. The summed derivative estimate is eta(t-s)<epsilon/2. Telescoping with the bad-tag bound proves constancy for every pair s<t.

Each coordinate indefinite L1 integral is AC and has the prescribed derivative under CC by the actual first L1 FTC. Subtracting it and the initial value preserves AC by the minimum of two half-tolerance moduli. Outside a finite union of null sets the difference has zero derivative. Scalar constancy gives every coordinate identity; the degenerate interval gives zero integral.

The reversed coefficients are essentially bounded and forcing is L2. Reversing finite interval families proves AC preservation; affine reflection preserves null sets and reverses the derivative sign. Every competing AC curve is coordinatewise continuous and bounded. Thus C qtilde is L1 and finite-horizon Cauchy–Schwarz gives g in L1. The new CC reconstruction lemma applies coordinatewise, discharging the previously missing integral equation.
